process.heading: How a herd treatment works
process.intro: From baseline assessment to a concrete plan of action — in five steps.

step1.title: Assess the herd
step1.description: A baseline assessment of hoof health across the entire herd.

step2.title: Treat the hooves
step2.description: All hooves are treated in the KVK800 hoof-trimming crush.

step3.title: Register findings
step3.description: Abnormalities are recorded digitally during trimming.

step4.title: Analyse the data
step4.description: The registered data is analysed afterwards, including by age and lactation stage.

step5.title: Advice & plan of action
step5.description: Based on the farm profile, a strategic plan is drawn up together with the farmer.

overview.title: Services
overview.description: From herd hoof care to tailored advice: NKGC supports dairy farmers in achieving structural hoof health.

herdTreatment.title: Herd hoof care
herdTreatment.heroLead: Good advice can only be given once every hoof has passed through our hands. A herd treatment gives the most complete picture of hoof health status on your farm.
herdTreatment.whyBody: Good advice is only possible with a complete picture of hoof health across the whole herd. By assessing and treating every animal during a herd treatment, a reliable baseline is created on which further policy can be based.
herdTreatment.kvkBody: NKGC works with KVK800 hoof-trimming crushes, designed with both the animal and the hoof trimmer in mind:

kvkPoints.noise: Low noise levels, keeping animals calmer
kvkPoints.comfort: Comfortable support using two belly bands
kvkPoints.flow: A low-stress approach via a waiting area and funnel system
kvkPoints.fixation: Secure fixation without joint strain while lifting
kvkPoints.ergonomic: Ergonomic for both animal and handler

herdTreatment.registrationBody: Abnormalities are recorded digitally during trimming, creating an up-to-date, complete overview of hoof health per animal.
herdTreatment.analysisBody: After the herd treatment, the registered data is analysed. This includes the animal, its age, lactation stage and the conditions recorded, to reveal patterns and points of attention within the herd.
herdTreatment.planBody: Based on the farm profile, a strategic plan of action is drawn up together with the dairy farmer. Depending on the findings, this may cover topics such as ration, management, barn layout, flooring, environment and concrete follow-up actions.
herdTreatment.collaborationBody: Where possible, other farm advisors are involved in carrying out the plan, such as the veterinarian, the nutritionist and the hoof trimmer, so actions are coordinated.
herdTreatment.youngStockBody: Hoof health in young stock also deserves structural attention, starting from their introduction into the dairy herd.
herdTreatment.youngStockCta: More about young stock hoof health
herdTreatment.ctaHeading: A herd treatment for your farm?
herdTreatment.ctaDescription: Get in touch to arrange a farm visit.

dairyHoofHealth.title: Dairy cattle hoof health
dairyHoofHealth.lead: Good advice can only be given once every hoof has passed through our hands. A herd treatment gives the best picture of hoof health status on your farm.
dairyHoofHealth.body1: NKGC works with KVK800 hoof-trimming crushes, designed for both animal comfort and a good working posture for the hoof trimmer: low noise levels, support in two belly bands and a low-stress approach.
dairyHoofHealth.body2: During the baseline assessment, all abnormalities are recorded digitally. The analysis looks at the animal, its age and lactation stage, to reveal links with specific conditions. Based on this farm profile, a strategic plan is drawn up together with the dairy farmer.
dairyHoofHealth.body3: Solutions differ per farm and can range from ration adjustments to management changes, or adjustments to barn layout or flooring.
dairyHoofHealth.body4: Other farm advisors — nutritionist, hoof trimmer, veterinarian — are involved where relevant, with a timeline for the planned actions.

youngStockHoofHealth.title: Young stock hoof health
youngStockHoofHealth.lead: NKGC believes hoof health in young stock deserves far more attention than it usually receives.
youngStockHoofHealth.whyBody: Good hoof shape and health matter when young stock is introduced into the dairy herd. In practice, however, hoof health in young stock often receives insufficient structural attention.
youngStockHoofHealth.issuesIntro: In young stock, NKGC regularly sees:
youngStockHoofHealth.approachBody: These issues can be addressed effectively with a planned approach. By signalling problems early and working structurally on hoof health, young stock starts out with a good foundation within the dairy herd.
youngStockHoofHealth.relationBody: Hoof health in young stock doesn't stand on its own: a good start lays the foundation for hoof health later in the dairy herd. That's why attention to young stock is part of a complete herd treatment.
youngStockHoofHealth.cta: Discuss the hoof health of your young stock

advice.title: Advice & guidance
advice.lead: In addition to herd hoof care, NKGC offers more extensive, second-line advice when an issue reaches beyond the hoof alone.
advice.whenHeading: When is more extensive advice useful?
advice.whenBody: When hoof problems keep recurring or are linked to management, nutrition, barn layout or environment, a more extensive advisory process can be valuable.
advice.whatIntro: During an advisory visit, NKGC maps the current situation, looking among other things at:

whatItems.situation: The current situation on the farm
whatItems.animals: Selected animals and their hoof health
whatItems.environment: The environment in which the animals are kept
whatItems.lyingBehaviour: Lying behaviour, where relevant measured with dedicated HOBO data loggers
whatItems.economics: The economic aspects of the current situation

advice.practicalBody: NKGC's advice is explicitly meant to be applicable in practice, tailored to the farm's specific situation.
advice.economicsBody: Where possible, NKGC provides an economic estimate of current costs and expected returns of an approach. This is an estimate based on the farm situation, not a guarantee.
advice.followUpBody: Advice is not necessarily a one-off visit. Follow-up can consist of a further visit, a phone consultation or additional guidance, with a timeline for the proposed actions.
advice.collaborationBody: Other farm advisors, such as the nutritionist, the hoof trimmer and the veterinarian, are involved where relevant.

overview.title: About NKGC
overview.lead: The Dutch Hoof Health Centre was founded from the wish to take the next step in high-quality care and advice around cattle hoof health.
overview.missionQuote: Bringing together and exchanging the knowledge and expertise of all stakeholders in dairy farming in the field of cattle hoof health, with the shared goal of reducing and preventing hoof disorders and improving animal welfare.
overview.historyBody1: NKGC was founded more than fifteen years ago from the wish to advance hoof health care and guidance within cattle veterinary medicine. The idea originated with Marcel Drint of Wellensiek Dierenartsen, who had long wanted to specialise further in dairy cattle hoof health.
overview.historyBody2: This idea grew into a partnership with Gerben Meerema of DAP West-Betuwe and Jan Lievaart, affiliated with DairySkills and Charles Sturt University. Driven by the belief that specialisation is needed to make real progress, they combined their knowledge and experience.
overview.historyBody3: Today, NKGC works daily with two veterinarians and a dedicated group of hoof trimmers on cattle hoof health, throughout the Netherlands.
